findings.finding: Existing snapshot IDs first load into STAGING from ACTIVE; only actually missing entries create a MissingMappingsEvent on MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS. After processing, frozen new data can be injected, STAGING validated/copied to ACTIVE, baked, and remap/objectholder notifications fired. An annotated compiled handler alone does not prove that a real saved legacy ID reaches it.

findings.boundary: Recognized mapping is alias plus registered object
findings.finding: REMAP removes the key from missing, attempts registration under the target canonical name with the old numeric ID, and adds old-key to target-name alias. The alias is included in later registry snapshots; getValue/getRaw traverse aliases when no direct entry exists. This does not register a newly recreated healing behavior or copy a separate item implementation.

findings.boundary: Numeric ID preservation has a native caveat
findings.finding: If the exact target object is already registered under the target name, add returns its previous ID; occupied requested IDs can also select a free ID. The REMAP branch warns when the returned ID differs from the requested old ID. Do not claim exact numeric-ID preservation or warning-free migration from static code.

findings.boundary: Unresolved mappings are not accepted compatibility
findings.finding: Without a handler-supplied valid target, DEFAULT can create a registry dummy or append defaulted and block the numeric ID. Local-world logging may continue through unidentified entries; a non-crashing load is not proof that the old item survived. Validation needs actual item identity, count and NBT after load/save/reopen.

findings.boundary: Snapshot aliases do not eliminate required reload check
findings.finding: Snapshot aliases are copied into staging before loadIds. Missing ID detection consults the ACTIVE registry raw name-to-ID lookup, which does not traverse aliases, so saved alias presence alone is insufficient to prove that future loads avoid missing-mapping processing.
